page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this server features 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block reads and writes, at 44.77 GB/sec and 35.36 GB/sec respectively, but small-block cached reads are weak. Cryptographic capabilities are average, as demonstrated by the Passmark CPU encryption test and supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n2d-standard-4 is designed for general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded tasks. However, its weak multi-threaded decompression, low database operations score, and lack of local NVMe storage make it less optimal for heavy database deployments, complex software compilation, or high-throughput multi-threaded applications.
